title: Drawing the plan as a tree
idea: MEET: see a big task as a top goal with sub-jobs hanging under it. No code.

exercises.prompt: Think of a big task as a TOP goal with smaller jobs under it. For 'make breakfast', which is the TOP goal?
exercises.explanation: 'Make breakfast' is the whole goal at the top. The smaller jobs (toast, egg, juice) hang beneath it.

exercises.prompt: Under the goal 'make breakfast', which are reasonable SUB-jobs? (Pick all.)
exercises.explanation: Toast, egg, and juice are all parts of making breakfast. Washing the car belongs to a different goal.

exercises.prompt: A sub-job can itself be split into even smaller jobs if it's still too big.
exercises.explanation: Yes. 'Fry the egg' could split into crack, heat the pan, cook. You split until each piece is simple.

exercises.prompt: Order the sub-jobs under 'send a letter'.
exercises.explanation: Write it, seal it in an envelope, then post it. The sub-jobs still run in a sensible order.

exercises.prompt: In this tree picture, what sits at the very top?
exercises.explanation: The whole goal sits at the top. Everything below it is a smaller piece that helps reach that goal.

exercises.prompt: Match each top goal to one of its sub-jobs.
exercises.explanation: Each big goal breaks into named sub-jobs. The tree shows the goal on top and its parts underneath.

exercises.prompt: Why is the tree picture useful before coding?
options: It shows every sub-job you'll need, and the order
exercises.explanation: The tree lays out the parts and their order, so nothing is forgotten when you build each piece.

exercises.prompt: If you forget a sub-job in the plan, the finished task will be missing part of its work.
exercises.explanation: Right. The plan is a checklist. A missing branch means a missing job - the result won't be complete.

exercises.prompt: REVIEW: under the goal 'report the class results', a sub-job is 'find the highest mark'. Its tool is...
options: max - track the biggest so far
exercises.explanation: 'Highest mark' is a track-the-best (max) job. Each branch of the tree maps to a tool you already know.

options: a clear list of named sub-jobs to solve one by one
exercises.explanation: The tree turns one scary goal into a tidy set of small jobs. Soon each named job becomes real code.
